segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 368 HKD is a genuinely cheap escape, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. I am keen for an optional break after six months without leisure travel, and this departure fits my window. Although Narita itself has little pull today, the low price makes the trip worthwhile, so I would still pay the 460 HKD normal fare if the member quota ran out.

analysis.summary: Eight of sixteen customers bought the 368 HKD member fare, generating 2944 HKD in basic receipts with no inventory denials. Buyers cited the fare as a strong bargain, several noting they would also pay the 460 HKD regular fare. Decliners split between four environment-forced cases (no available ticket within budget) and four low-interest optional-leisure cases where price was affordable but trip appeal was weak. The fare is already at its permitted cap, so no higher test is possible. Evidence supports retaining the current fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 368 HKD fare on fresh paired customers will reproduce roughly 40-50% weighted conversion, with declines driven mainly by low optional-trip interest and inventory/budget constraints rather than fare level. A materially lower conversion would contradict this.

Five declines were driven by low trip interest or a high outside option, not by the fare itself; three declines cited no available ticket within budget. No customer objected primarily to price. analysis.summary: At the current 350 HKD member fare, 9 of 15 customers bought and 6 declined. Four declines were forced by unavailable inventory within budget, not price; two were low-interest optional browsing. Buyers repeatedly cited the fare as compelling and said they would still pay the 460 HKD regular fare. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points toward testing a higher fare, though buying at today's price does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because current buyers report willingness to pay the 460 HKD regular fare.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

Most declines cite low trip interest, weak destination appeal, recent travel or optional-trip inertia rather than the fare itself; three declines are inventory/budget-forced. Buyers describe the fare as compelling value, and several would pay the 460 HKD regular fare. Since the current fare already sits at the cap, no upward test is possible; evidence does not support lowering the fare.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 368 HKD fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly 35-45% member conversion, with declines driven mainly by low interest or destination appeal rather than fare level; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 268 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought and 6 declined. Most buyers cited the low fare as the decisive trigger, several noting they would not pay the 460 HKD regular fare. All six declines were driven by low trip interest or a preferred free schedule, not by price; one decline was inventory-forced. No customer objected to the fare itself. This suggests the fare is already attractive and demand is limited mainly by interest, not price.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because most current buyers are fare-triggered but declines are interest-driven rather than price-driven.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 4 bought the 360 HKD fare and 12 declined. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections. Five declines cited low trip interest or keeping options open, and one cited low interest with high outside appeal. Only the four buyers cited the fare as compelling; two would also pay 460. No customer primarily objected to the fare itself, so evidence does not support lowering price. Current fare sits just below the 368 cap.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will not reduce conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because buyers cited the fare as a bargain and two accepted the 460 fallback.

analysis.summary: At the current 312 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought, generating 3120 HKD in basic receipts; 4 declines were inventory/budget-forced and 2 were low-interest optional-trip declines, not price objections. Several buyers cited the fare as decisive, and some would still pay the 460 HKD regular fare. The paired initial at 368 HKD showed lower revenue, but this is aggregate context only. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying today does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a member fare above 312 HKD on fresh customers will preserve enough member purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at least as high as at 312 HKD, since several buyers stated the regular fare remained acceptable.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At a 302 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain, several would still pay the 460 HKD regular fare. Declines were mainly low trip interest, recent travel, or optional-leisure preference rather than price objections; three were inventory/budget forced. No customer primarily objected to the fare itself. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 302 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh paired customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts versus 302 HKD, because most current buyers report willingness to pay the 460 HKD regular fare and few declines cite price.

analysis.summary: At the current 368 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Five declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and four were low-interest optional-trip browsers who found the fare affordable but the trip unappealing. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high; several buyers said they would also pay the 460 HKD regular fare. The fare is already at its permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed. assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
